orientation: A frozen eight-task campaign tested whether readiness signals plus replaceable spans improve deferred composition. The method beat hole-only in 5/8 comparisons, but unrestricted full revision won 8/8 while using less latency and fewer generated tokens; the labnote rejects readiness-span for production.
finding: Readiness plus whole-span repair partially improved on hole-only, but lost every blinded comparison against unrestricted full revision and was rejected as a production composition mechanism.
limitations: The result comes from eight authored tasks judged by one reviewer and is not a general population estimate.
The campaign evaluated one model at temperature zero under the frozen protocol.
Two apparatus pilots failed before the valid campaign and were excluded from review.
negative_evidence: Full revision was preferred to readiness-span in all eight comparisons.
Readiness-span used more latency and generated tokens and frequently repeated or contradicted source material.
The disposition explicitly rejects production adoption and repetition with a larger token budget.
evidence_quotes: Readiness-span was preferred to hole-only in five of eight cases; hole-only won three, with no ties.
Full revision was preferred to readiness-span in all eight cases, with no ties.
Because one reviewer judged a small authored corpus, this remains a bounded result rather than a general population estimate.
Do not add it to the production composition path and do not repeat this corpus with a larger token budget.
